text:
sara_support: CraftCo opened a ticket — autopay invoices failing intermittently. Merchant sees two different decline reasons in our dashboard: `insufficient_funds` and `fraud_suspected`. Happening across 6 invoices in last 12h. Customer says 3DS challenge never shows up on their checkout (mobile web). :frowning_face:

craftco_ops: Yup, we're seeing the popup get stuck on a white screen on iOS Safari. Some customers report a network error, others get 'authentication failed'.

annie_ops: Do we have gateway request ids for the failed attempts? Can you paste one sample event here (request_id / acquirer_code / acs_url if present)?

craftco_ops: example: req_9f3a2b, acquirer_code=A3, gateway_code=402_3DS_REQ, acs_url=https://acs.example.com/challenge/xyz

payments-bot: Charge failed for invoice inv_4472: reason=insufficient_funds, gateway_request=req_9f3a2b, attempt=1, payment_method=card_ending_4242, region=eu-west-1

tomas_prod_eng: Quick checklist: 1) Is the 3DS iframe/cross-origin cookie blocked? 2) Are we returning the ACS URL to the client properly? 3) Any 3rd-party CSP or iframe sandbox on CraftCo site? Can you repro with a desktop and capture network tab?

craftco_ops: We reproduced on iPhone Safari — network tab shows POST /start_challenge returns 200 with payload `{ "acs_url": "https://acs.example.com/challenge/xyz" }` then the iframe `about:blank` and never loads the ACS. No obvious JS exceptions.

annie_ops: This smells like SameSite cookie / third-party cookie block. Mobile Safari blocks third-party cookies for iframes which can prevent ACS from rendering. If ACS needs cookies, it fails and fallback becomes issuer decline/fraud.

tomas_prod_eng: Can you grab a HAR and the full response headers from the start_challenge response? We need to check `Set-Cookie` and `X-Frame-Options` and CSP. Also paste our gateway logs for req_9f3a2b — looking for acquirer flags (fingerprint_mismatch / high_risk_score).

craftco_ops: HAR attached in the ticket. From our side: no X-Frame-Options, CSP allows frames from acs.example.com. Response headers: `Set-Cookie: __acs=...; SameSite=Lax` — ah.

sara_support: That SameSite=Lax would indeed prevent the cookie being sent in a third-party iframe on navigation from a cross-site context. Suggest asking ACS vendor if they can use SameSite=None; Secure. For an immediate workaround, merchant can try redirect flow instead of iframe.

tomas_prod_eng: On our side, gateway logs for req_9f3a2b show: `fraud_score=78, device_fingerprint_missing=true, acquirer_action=challenge_requested, final_status=decline_fraud` — we auto-fell back to decline when ACS didn't complete.

annie_ops: Action items: - Ask merchant to switch to redirect (temporary) and re-run autopay test - We create an internal ticket to map ACS timeouts to a clearer status so merchant sees "3DS not completed" instead of generic fraud/insufficient_funds - Payments team to add retry policy for transient ACS failures (can try later before final decline).

craftco_ops: Trying redirect now, will update. Thanks.

payments-bot: Created internal issue PAY-1129: map-acs-timeout-to-3ds-not-completed (assigned to tomas_prod_eng).

craftco_ops: Redirect flow worked for one test charge, customer completed challenge and charge succeeded. We'll plan to ship redirect fallback. :white_check_mark:

sara_support: Great. Marking as mitigation found. I'll follow up to confirm the remaining failed invoices are retried per their billing policy. Also advising we update docs with a note about SameSite pitfalls and mobile ACs.

tomas_prod_eng: I will file a small runtime change to surface the ACS failure reason in logs and UI. Low-risk patch.

annie_ops: Closing loop for now — reopen if we see more failures after merchant enables redirect fallback.

craftco_ops: Thanks team!
